meta.method: Judged all 240 claims (na-c-001 to na-c-240; all are claims, no events in this range) against their cited sources, not just quote existence. For each item I read the statement, notes, dates, authority and coordinates, then read the quoted text in context in the cached pages (.cache/fetch) and grepped the cached full pages for date bounds, month/day precision and conflicting statements. The 94 citations marked unfetchable (Wikipedia pages with accented titles, The Canadian Encyclopedia, mptn-nsn.gov) were re-fetched myself via the Wikipedia API and Wayback copies and checked the same way. Items were marked partially-verified when a date bound or month/day was inferred or absent from the cited text, a placeholder start (not the window-start convention for pre-contact homelands) or a general date was applied to a specific place, sources conflict, authority is stronger than the text, or the coordinate is an admitted centroid or anchor for a region. No item had a core claim contradicted, so none was rejected; no item was left unverified.

na-c-016.note: Re-fetched Wikipedia: bombardment forced Itza defenders to abandon Nojpeten; fell 13 March 1697 (last Maya kingdom).

na-c-017.note: Wikipedia (re-fetched): Chi and Pat attacked Tepich 30 July 1847; by spring 1848 Maya held most of Yucatan except Campeche and Merida.

na-c-018.note: Yucatan Today: capital from Oct 1850 to end of war; troops took it 3 May 1901; Wikipedia 1901 occupation. Month precision fits.

na-c-022.note: Quote only calls Tilantongo an 'ancient capital'; 1521 subjugation is quoted. 1492 start is a window placeholder (author admits) and no source shows Tilantongo governing La Mixteca in 1492.

na-c-023.note: Wikipedia: Aztec defeat of Mixtecs 1458, fort at Huaxyacac 1486 for tribute, Orozco reached Oaxaca valley 25 Nov 1521.

na-c-025.note: Wikipedia (re-fetched): Mixton War 1540-1542, Tenamaztle of Nochistlan, Alvarado repulsed June 1541, stronghold fell early 1542.

na-c-026.note: Wikipedia and Indigenous Mexico: survivors of Mixton enslaved and transported from Apozol and Juchipila to Guadalajara and haciendas.

na-c-034.note: Wikipedia (re-fetched): revolt began 16 Nov 1616 at Santa Catarina, crushed/ended 1620; ~100 killed at Santiago Papasquiaro and at El Zape.

na-c-175.note: TCE (archived): Yellowknives briefly occupied the Yellowknife River region, displacing Tlicho until 1823 retaliation. 'Early 19th century' rendered as decade 1800.

na-c-176.note: Wikipedia Tlicho and Treaty 8: Yellowknives and Tlicho under Drygeese signed at Fort Resolution in 1900 (adhesion 25 July 1900).

na-c-177.note: TCE (archived) Chipewyan and Yellowknives: occupied Yellowknife River region in early 19th c., Tlicho retaliated 1823.

na-c-178.note: TCE (archived): Drygeese met Treaty Commissioner 1900; Wikipedia Treaty 8: adhesion 25 July 1900 at Fort Resolution.

na-c-179.note: TCE (archived): Peel's River Post founded 1840 to trade with Gwich'in; moved 1848-49 on Red Leggings's recommendation.

na-c-180.note: TCE Gwich'in: HBC established Fort Yukon in 1847; Gwich'yaa Gwich'in at Fort Yukon. Start year is the post.

na-c-181.note: Wikipedia Tadoussac: Cartier in 1535 found Innu using it as a base for seal hunting.

na-c-182.note: Wikipedia Mashteuiatsh: home of Pekuakamiulnuatsh; became an Indian Act reserve in 1856. Start year is reserve creation.

na-c-183.note: Wikipedia Sheshatshiu: HBC post at North West River 1836; earlier used by Innu as coastal settlement and trading place. Start year is the post.

na-c-184.note: Haudenosaunee site and Onondaga Nation support Onondaga as Keepers of the Fire and main meeting place. The 1142 date is not in any cited quote and the author concedes the founding date is contested (time immemorial vs mid-16th c.).

na-c-185.note: Wikipedia: Cayuga lived between Owasco and Cayuga lakes; TCE: Haudenosaunee in New York by c.500-600 CE. That date is not Cayuga-specific, and the 1789 end is not in these quotes (and Cayuga kept land afterwards).

na-c-186.note: Wikipedia Sullivan Expedition: after the 1788 Phelps-Gorham purchase, 'the following year' Cayuga ceded most territory except ~64,000 acres. Cayuga Nation article ties reservation to 1794, disclosed.

na-c-187.note: Wikipedia Ganondagan: largest Seneca village of the 17th century; Seneca Nation: Finger Lakes and Genesee Valley. 1687 burning ends it.

na-c-188.note: Wikipedia: Denonville's army reached Ganondagan 13-14 July 1687 and found it burned by the Seneca. This is a temporary flight and the Seneca stayed in the region, so 'removed' with an open end overstates.

na-c-189.note: Wikipedia Treaty of Big Tree: negotiated 20 Aug-16 Sept 1797, Seneca relinquished nearly all of western New York except twelve reservations.

na-c-190.note: Wikipedia Buffalo Creek Reservation: Sayenqueraghta settled Seneca, Cayuga and Onondaga there after 1779; reservation dissolved after 1842 treaty.

na-c-191.note: Wikipedia Buffalo Creek Reservation: 1838 treaty required cession and removal west; Senate ratified replacement treaty 1842; only reservation dissolved, Seneca kept four others.

na-c-192.note: Wikipedia: most NY Mohawks lived at Canajoharie (Upper Castle) in the Mohawk Valley. The 600 CE start is a general Haudenosaunee-in-New-York archaeological date, not Mohawk or Canajoharie specific.

na-c-193.note: Wikipedia Mohawk: Upper Castle Mohawks fled to Fort Niagara, Lower Castle to near Montreal; Americans forced cession of NY territories. Decade precision fits.

na-c-194.note: Wikipedia Haldimand Proclamation: issued 25 Oct 1784; TCE (archived): six miles each side of the Grand River, relocation 1784.

na-c-195.note: TCE (archived): Six Nations territory shrank through leases and sales; final reduction in 1847 left 5 per cent of Haldimand lands.

na-c-196.note: Wikipedia: Oneida around Oneida Lake held ~6 million acres in early 17th c., reduced to 32 acres by 1830s. Oneida Lake point is flagged approximate for a county-scale homeland.

na-c-197.note: Wikipedia: early 1800s NY State and speculators forced Oneida land sales. Point is the approximate Oneida Lake anchor for a region-wide cession.

na-c-198.note: Wikipedia Oneida: many Oneida relocated to Wisconsin in the 1820s-30s under removal pressure. Point is an approximate lake anchor.

na-c-199.note: Wikipedia Oneida Nation: relocated to NE Wisconsin from the 1820s; 1838 treaty reservation; stayed when asked in 1845 to move.

na-c-200.note: Delaware Nation and Wikipedia: Lenapehoking encompassed the Delaware and Lehigh valleys; 1492 is a placeholder start; ends with 1737 Walking Purchase.

na-c-201.note: Wikipedia and Delaware Nation: Walking Purchase walk on 19 Sept 1737, deed claiming 1,200,000 acres, 'a little over a million acres' taken.

na-c-202.note: Wikipedia Coshocton: Lenape village established late 1770s, destroyed by Brodhead April 1781.

na-c-203.note: Delaware Nation: moved from Ohio to Indiana, Missouri, Kansas, Arkansas, Texas, Oklahoma between 1778 and 1830. The 1781 start is the author's approximation for a decades-long series of treaties.

na-c-204.note: Wikipedia Gnadenhutten: founded Oct 1772 as Moravian Lenape settlement; Delaware Nation: 96 killed 8 March 1782.

na-c-205.note: Wikipedia: Delaware ancestors agreed in 1867 to relocate to Cherokee Nation in Indian Territory; tribe based at Bartlesville (present seat is an anchor).

na-c-206.note: Delaware Nation: Absentee Delaware finally moved to Wichita allotments at Anadarko around 1873.

na-c-207.note: Virginia Places and Wikipedia: Powhatan seat at Werowocomoco when English arrived 1607; Orapax capital by Nov 1609.

na-c-208.note: Wikipedia Anglo-Powhatan Wars: Jamestown May 1607 in Powhatan territory; peace treaty with Necotowance October 1646 ended the third war.

na-c-209.note: Wikipedia and Virginia Places: Oct 1646 treaty, Necotowance vacated the peninsula between York and James and stayed north of the York.

na-c-210.note: Pamunkey Tribe: living on the reservation land at least 15,000 years (tribal claim); reservation established 1646; never ceded.

na-c-211.note: Mashpee site, Wikipedia: Massasoit lived at Sowams (Pokanoket); Wampanoag effectively landless after King Philip's War; Metacom killed 12 Aug 1676.

na-c-212.note: Wikipedia: Pokanoket at Bristol/Warren; Plymouth/Massachusetts troops destroyed the Mount Hope town 28 June 1675; Mashpee site on long habitation.

na-c-213.note: Wikipedia Patuxet: Wampanoag band; all but Tisquantum died before Pilgrims landed 1620.

na-c-214.note: Mashpee Wampanoag site: inhabited area 12,000+ years; re-acknowledged 2007; reservation 2015. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-215.note: Aquinnah tribal site: continuous connection to homelands for thousands of years; Wampanoag Nation covered SE Massachusetts and E Rhode Island.

na-c-216.note: Wikipedia: Narragansett controlled the land west of Narragansett Bay; Encyclopedia.com: about 11,000 years, as few as 200 left by summer 1676. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-217.note: Wikipedia Great Swamp Fight: battle 19 Dec 1675 in South Kingstown; survivors sold into slavery, executed or fled. NPS corroborates December 1675.

na-c-218.note: Encyclopedia.com: small independent unit on a reservation in southern New England for 200+ years before 1880; Wikipedia: Charlestown is reservation location. Start circa 1676.

na-c-219.note: Encyclopedia.com and Wikipedia: Rhode Island purchased the reservation in 1880, detribalization 1880-84; 1,800 acres transferred 1978.

na-c-220.note: Encyclopedia.com: Pequot lands covered SE Connecticut; Wikipedia: Mystic attack 26 May 1637. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-221.note: Wikipedia: 400-700 killed at Mystic, survivors captured as slaves/servants; Treaty of Hartford forbade Pequot towns.

na-c-222.note: Wikipedia Treaty of Hartford: 21 Sept 1638 treaty barred Pequots from their lands and name. The 1666 end uses Wikipedia's Mashantucket reservation date, which the same article contradicts (1683); author flags this.

na-c-223.note: Wikipedia lead gives Mashantucket reservation 1666 but the same article says Connecticut established the two reservations in 1683. Start year is internally contested; federal recognition 1983 is quoted.

na-c-224.note: Wikipedia Fort Shantok: principal Mohegan settlement 1636-1682; Encyclopedia.com: Mohegans allied with English in the 1637 Pequot War.

na-c-225.note: Wikipedia Mohegan: Land Controversy in British courts from 1704; Encyclopedia.com: Mason land case decided against the Mohegan in 1767.

na-c-226.note: Encyclopedia.com: individual allotments began 1790; Mohegan Church founded 1831. Start year is the allotment date, not residence start (disclosed).

na-c-227.note: Wikipedia dates Confederacy formation to the 1680s; TCE (archived): politically active at least from contact. Point is an admitted approximate centre of Dawnland, not a seat (confederacy has no capital).

na-c-228.note: Wikipedia Norridgewock: Rale's Jesuit mission from 1694; village raided Aug 1724 (Battle of Norridgewock).

na-c-229.note: Wikipedia Battle of Norridgewock: escapees forced to abandon village and moved north to Odanak; New Englanders settled the lower Kennebec.

na-c-230.note: Wikipedia Odanak: new settlement established 1700; Abenaki settled Odanak early 18th c.; Norridgewock survivors moved there.

na-c-231.note: Wabanaki Alliance: Penobscot ancestral homeland in the Penobscot River drainage; seat of government on Indian Island above Old Town Falls. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-232.note: Wabanaki Alliance: Penobscot cessions in 1796, 1818, 1833; retained only the river and islands from Indian Island north.

na-c-233.note: Canada (RCAANC): Passamaquoddy along the St. Croix River; occupation at least 2,500-3,000 years. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-234.note: Wabanaki Alliance: Passamaquoddy cessions in 1794 to Massachusetts. Point is an approximate anchor on the bay (flagged by author) for a large cession area.

na-c-235.note: RCAANC: Maliseet along the St. John River valley; Wikipedia: Meductic largest Wolastoqiyik settlement until 18th century; 1720s church. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-236.note: TCE (archived) and RCAANC: Mi'kmaq in Mi'gma'gi 10,000+ years, seven districts incl. Unama'ki; Cape Breton main community before 1500. Eskasoni is an anchor.

na-c-237.note: RCAANC: Jean-Baptiste Cope chief sakamow of Shubenacadie; Wikipedia Dummer's War: Saint Anne's mission at Shubenacadie. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-238.note: DCB Membertou: settled near Port-Royal probably as early as mid-16th c.; took charge of Port-Royal; died there 18 Sept 1611. 'Perhaps in St Marys Bay' is a caveat.

na-c-239.note: TCE (archived): Mi'kmaq inhabited Gaspe and Maritimes, seven districts incl. Gespe'gewa'gi, 10,000+ years. 1492 is a placeholder start.

na-c-240.note: RCAANC: Mi'kmaq anger at Halifax settlement of June 1749, intermittent warfare until 1751; Wikipedia: Cornwallis founded Halifax 21 June 1749.
